updates.statement: Most of the early wall-time reduction came from cutting the epochs needed to reach 75%, through the backbone and averaging choices: the airbench96 port, Muon, Lookahead and wd ×0.5. Together with resizing, compile, averaging and stem backward truncation they give about 11x over the organizer's 40-epoch ResNet9 baseline (59.30 s on an A100 80GB PCIe, taken from forks and not run in this loop). That is 5.31 s at the E036 tip, which passed the local bar on only 1 of 3 builds of the same commit (0.7532, 0.7525, 0.7497). No accuracy-per-epoch booster has held up since E016: E022, E025, E029, E030, E032 and E044 were null or negative, and E013/E014 were underpowered. Every keep since E016 cut per-step cost (H2) or spent margin (H4). Any further sample-efficiency gain probably needs a structural change (H1.7), not more scalar sweeps.
updates.reason: Review: the 'main lever' claim no longer matches recent evidence, and the headline numbers were stale (1 of 3 builds, not 1 of 2). Confidence lowered for current decisions; the settled historical gains stay supported.

updates.statement: In short CIFAR-100 runs, end-of-run averaging is a first-order lever: Lookahead/EMA gave +0.97 pp at E005. The airbench Lookahead schedule is a local optimum on both sides. A harder pull hurt (E025, −0.27 pp held-out), longer free runs hurt (E030, −0.24 pp), and dropping LS late hurt (E032, −0.23 pp), so LS 0.3 regularizes what gets averaged. With averaging on, the final-LR floor does not matter (E009, C0021). Recomputing the BN statistics of the averaged weights adds nothing (E044 paired test: K=3 −0.003 pp, 9/20 seeds positive), so the gain comes from the averaged weights, not from the BN-statistics mixture. The reset may carry part of the gain (Switch-EMA, C0024). Untested: plain EMA (H1.3.5).
updates.reason: E044 refuted BN recalibration in a clean paired design. The BN-mixture caveat is removed, as the review suggested.

E044-: paired, trajectory-identical test on seeds 13–32. K=3 gave −0.003 pp (9/20 positive) and K=1 gave −0.105 pp, against a predicted ≥+0.15 pp. The test is noise-free with respect to trajectory, so one result is decisive.
E044 showed BN recalibration at 32 px recovers nothing on the tip, which lowers the prior that E018's loss was a BN-calibration effect.
No change in evidence. E043 caps the Muon time overhead at ~2.5% of a step (NS plus head GEMM ≈0.85 ms of 33.5 ms), so the remaining question is accuracy (the E006 confound), not time.

updates.statement: On the E036 tip, replace Muon on the conv filters with Nesterov SGD (lr and wd scaled for batch 2000, everything else unchanged). Prediction: the 20-seed unselected mean (seeds 13–32, same-build baseline) drops by at least 0.3 pp and time falls by about 2% (the NS share measured in E043). If the loss is under 0.15 pp, E006's gain came from batch size or the RNG re-draw.
updates.reason: E043 measured NS at ~2.5% of step time, so the time upside is capped below 3%. The test's only real value is resolving E006's confound; it was rebased onto the tip and the unselected-seed protocol.
E043: NS plus head GEMM is ~2.5% of a step. Cutting iterations (e.g. 5→3, or Turbo-Muon's −1) saves at most ~1%, below the 1.5% threshold and below build noise. Retired without a run.
Search: the airbench paper finds alternating flip's effective speedup is largest without TTA (~27% at 20 epochs). Indirect support; untested here.

Since E016, no scalar sweep (E022, E029, E030, E032) has produced a held-out gain. Search adds Hiverge's untested deltas (LS 0.09, jitter, SiLU) and ghost BN (new child), but the recipe looks at a flat optimum for scalars.

Search: reference airbench94_muon renormalizes every conv filter to norm sqrt(out_channels) after each step, so filter wd is inert if the port kept that line. Settle by reading the port's code; no run needed.

updates.statement: At a fixed epoch count, the cost per epoch (systems overhead plus per-layer cost per sample) is a large lever. Levers found so far: compile/fusion (−14%, E004); progressive resizing (−22% E007, −2.9% E026, −3.2% E033); and stem backward truncation, made up of a group-1 freeze over the last 25% of steps (−8.8% with no held-out cost, E028, stacked in E034) and a whitening-bias detach after 20% of steps (−2.4%, E036). Launch overhead is exhausted (E015, E017; Fable's CIFAR-10 record agrees). The E043 profile of the 32 px step (33.5 ms): conv fwd/wgrad/dgrad 66%, memory-bound fused BN/GELU/pointwise 27%, NS plus head ~2.5%. The conv kernels already run at high throughput (H2.2.4), so the remaining per-step levers are the memory-bound share (H6.5) and further backward truncation (H2.6, H6.6). Limits: freezing from 60% costs about 0.4–0.56 pp (E037); folding BN in the frozen phase saves nothing (E039); a group-2 freeze for the last 10% saved 4.4% but read −0.14 pp (E046, inconclusive).
updates.reason: Folded in the E043 profile, E046, and the outside replication that systems work is exhausted.

updates.statement: Removing kernel-launch and Python overhead speeds up each step without changing the math. Compile plus a fused optimizer gave −14% (E004). After that the step is GPU-bound: CUDA graphs gave −0.9% (E015) and removing graph breaks −0.5% (E017), matching Fable's CIFAR-10 finding that whole-run CUDA graphs gave nothing measurable. Side effect: E015's max-autotune/cudagraph build made rebuilds non-reproducible (3-seed spread up to 0.35 pp, H4.1), so its −0.9% may not be worth what it costs in reproducibility (H4.1.5).
updates.reason: Search (Fable) confirms the lever is exhausted. Review: E015's keep introduced the build lottery.

Settled by calculation from E043, no run needed. Analytic conv MACs at 32 px are ≈0.45 GMAC per sample forward (group 1 ≈93M, group 2 ≈230M, group 3 ≈129M), so a batch-2000 fwd+bwd step is ≈5 TFLOP against ~22 ms of conv kernel time. That implies ≥150–240 TFLOP/s, well above the 90 TFLOP/s threshold even if the count is off by 1.5x. The implied value exceeds airbench's quoted 112, so the FLOP count should be checked against the code, but the conclusion holds: no conv kernel-efficiency lever >5% remains.

updates.statement: The 24 px bridge is dispensable. On the E036 tip, running 20/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps (E040's schedule) cuts mean time by at least 2% and loses no more than 0.1 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean (seeds 13–32) vs E036 measured on the same seeds in the same build session. E040's −0.28 pp was against E036's selection seeds. The earlier '−0.09 pp vs fresh seeds' compared different seed sets and is withdrawn.
updates.reason: Review: the −0.09 pp figure compared E040 on seeds 3–12 with E036 on seeds 13–22, which is invalid. Needs a same-seed rerun.
Proxy-based selection adds forward passes to a GPU-bound step. Members expect refutation 3–0. The proxy-free variant lives under H2.7.
Retired with H2.4: the extra selection forward costs more than it saves on a GPU-bound step, and H2.7.1 tests the cheaper proxy-free version.

updates.statement: Truncating the backward pass at the high-resolution stem cuts per-step cost far more than its FLOP share, at little accuracy cost if the stem has trained at 32 px. Evidence: freezing group 1 and the whitening bias for the last 25% of steps saved ~23% per frozen 32 px step (E043: 7.7 of 33.5 ms, nearly half of it in memory-bound fused kernels) with no held-out loss (E028), and it stacked with +0.5 epoch (E034). Detaching the whitening output after 20% of steps saved a further 2.4% with no held-out loss (E036). Limits: a freeze from 60% cost 0.4–0.56 pp (E037); a conv1-only freeze from 60% saved 0.9% for −0.21 pp (E042); folding frozen group-1 BN saved nothing (E039); a group-2 freeze over the last 10% saved 4.4% for −0.14 pp against a cross-build baseline (E046, inconclusive).
updates.reason: Added E042, E043 and E046. The core claim still rests on E028/E034/E036.

E046~: −4.4% time; seeds 13–32 −0.14 pp vs E044 k0, which is a separately built copy, so rebuild noise is missing from the ~0.08 pp SE. Between the thresholds. Members are split (2 supported, 1 refuted), so the decisive test is H2.6.9: a same-build baseline plus a top-up arm.

Review: I044 says the run was on E023 (225 steps) but it was compared with E027. Both the −10.7% time and −0.27 pp figures may use the wrong reference. E031's time beat every forecast, which is also unexplained (ragged-batch drop and phase-fraction shifts are candidates). Check commit 4c9a872 and retest as H2.7.1.

updates.statement: The binding constraint is the accuracy margin. The best time comes from sitting just above the 0.753 3-seed bar while still holding ≥0.75 over 40 seeds. The E036 tip is weaker than earlier estimates. Its only unselected 20-seed estimate (E044 k0, seeds 13–32) is ~0.7535. Across three builds its seeds 0–2 mean averaged 0.7518 (0.7532, 0.7525, 0.7497), and seed 1 runs persistently low, so its local pass probability is ≤50%. The 40-seed official bar has ~0.35 pp headroom. Gate, fixed from now on: a 20-seed mean ≥0.7545 on unselected seeds against a same-build baseline, plus seeds 0–2 ≥0.753 in the same build. Every override must be logged. Margin should be bought (H4.2.6) before any further time cut.
updates.reason: Review: the headline numbers were stale (the pooled 0.7547 includes selection seeds). Rebuilt around the unselected estimate and a fixed gate.

updates.statement: Accuracy noise has four parts. (a) Rebuild noise: builds without cudagraphs are bit-identical per seed (E003=E004, E010=E012). Max-autotune/cudagraph rebuilds re-draw kernels: per-seed shifts are 0.1–0.44 pp, and the 3-seed mean spread reached 0.35 pp across three builds of E036 (0.7532/0.7525/0.7497), against ±0.03 in E019. Cross-build comparisons must include this noise. (b) Seed and test-set noise: per-seed std is 0.15–0.35 pp. (c) Trajectory re-draw with a persistent component: math or RNG changes re-draw trajectories, but seed 1 was lowest of seeds 0–2 in 10 of 11 runs from E036 to E046 (~0.3 pp below seeds 0 and 2), probably through the init, which is fixed whenever the architecture is. So the seeds 0–2 mean is biased about −0.15 pp, not merely noisy. (d) Selection: seeds 3–12 sit 0.19 pp above 13–22 for E036 (~1.5σ), either winner's curse or seed-set difficulty (H4.4). Changes worth <0.25 pp need 20 seeds per arm, measured against a same-build baseline on unselected seeds.
updates.reason: E043 broke the '<0.1 pp across rebuilds' claim. The review found the persistent seed-1 deficit and that the winner's curse is ambiguous.

E043-: a third build of the unchanged E036 commit read 0.7497, against 0.7532 (E036) and 0.7525 (E038). The 3-seed mean spread is 0.35 pp, outside the predicted ≤0.25 pp. E019's ±0.03 was a lucky small sample.

updates.statement: Near the tip, true epochs are a smooth dial, but its slope is stale. The pre-freeze held-out points 9.5: 0.7570, 9.0: 0.7556, 8.5: 0.7533 give ~0.37–0.44 pp per epoch (quoted inconsistently) at ~0.68 s per epoch, so about 1.5–2.7 s/pp. The tip's per-epoch cost is lower (freeze, detach, 20 px), so both numbers need re-measuring on E036 with unselected seeds (H4.2.6). Convention: boosters are ranked by cost per pp, cuts by saving per pp. On that convention E045 (+0.20 s for +0.135 pp ≈1.5 s/pp) ties the dial rather than losing to it. E028's freeze (≥5 s/pp) is the only lever clearly better than the dial; E018, E024 and E021 are clearly worse. Rank against the dial only when the intervals separate.
updates.reason: Review: the dial slope was measured on pre-freeze bases and quoted inconsistently, and E045's rate arithmetic was wrong and inverted. Confidence in using it for rankings lowered until it is re-measured.

updates.statement: Local SXM4 results transfer to the PCIe judge only partly. Search: the PCIe card has a 300 W cap (vs 400 W), ~5% less memory bandwidth and the same fp16 peak, so judged absolute times should come in ~5–10% higher. The lever ranking should mostly hold: bandwidth-bound levers (stem truncation, about half memory-bound per E043) lose ~5% of their saving, and compute-bound ones may lose more to power throttling. The accuracy risk comes from the population mean (~0.7535 unselected) and from build-to-build kernel reselection on the judge's own build, which E043 shows can move the 3-seed mean by up to 0.35 pp.
updates.reason: Search gave PCIe vs SXM4 specs. E043 enlarged the rebuild-noise estimate.

updates.statement: Comparisons against a just-kept tip's selection seeds (3–12) may be biased against the challenger by up to ~0.2 pp (E036: 0.7557 on 3–12 vs 0.7538 on 13–22). That gap rests on one ~1.5σ comparison, and seed-set difficulty (13–32 harder than 3–12) explains it equally well. Until H4.4.2 separates the two, post-hoc discounts on E040, E041 and E042 should not be applied, and all baselines must come from the same unselected seeds in the same build.
updates.reason: Review: single 1.5σ comparison with an alternative explanation. Confidence lowered and a decisive test added.

updates.statement: Early in training (the 20/24 px phases), accuracy is carried by the number of optimizer steps under the LR warm-up and peak, not by the pixels processed. Lowering resolution there at a fixed step count is nearly free (E026, E033), while removing steps costs about as much as a uniform trim (E031, E041, both noise-ambiguous). E045 (batch 1000 in the 20 px phase) read +0.135 pp for +0.20 s (≈1.5 s/pp, the same as the dial, ~1.7σ against a cross-build baseline). Corollary: the cheap time levers are those that cut per-step cost at a fixed step count.
updates.reason: E045 rate corrected to ~1.5 s/pp (review). Direction consistent with H5.2 but within noise once rebuild noise is added.

updates.statement: The per-MAC cost of the step is not uniform across layers, so a systems or architecture lever worth ≥5% may remain at near-identical math. The E043 profile (32 px, 33.5 ms) shows the conv kernels at high throughput (H2.2.4) but memory-bound fused BN/GELU/pointwise kernels at 27% of the step. Freezing the stem saved 7.7 ms, of which 3.5 ms was fused kernels, against a ~12% FLOP share. So the non-uniformity is mostly elementwise traffic on large activations (H6.3, H6.5, H6.6), not tensor-core inefficiency. NVIDIA guidance and E043 weaken the Cin=24 alignment story (H6.4). The 24 px step costs 0.56x a 32 px step (pixel-proportional), so small maps are not the issue at tile-friendly sizes (H6.1 refuted).
updates.reason: The statement said no profile had been run; E043 ran one. Rewritten around its findings.

E043: the 24 px full step is 18.7 ms vs 33.5 ms at 32 px (ratio 0.56, the pixel ratio 0.5625), and Fable measured 0.56x too. There is no throughput drop at small tile-friendly maps. E021's sublinear scaling is better explained by the 320-channel width (H6.2).
E043-: step time at 24 px scales with pixels relative to 32 px, so layer-weighted throughput at 24 px is not ≥20% lower. The group-3 per-layer part was not measured.

E043+: non-GEMM work is ~31% of the 32 px step. The stem freeze saved 7.7 ms (23% of the step) against ~12% of step FLOPs, and 3.5 ms of that was fused memory-bound kernels. Lavin (search) gives outside support. Members vote 3 supported.
E043 confirms the first half (non-GEMM ≥30%: 31%). The second half (group 1 plus whitening ≥35% of the step) was not measured per layer, so the prediction stays open pending a per-layer breakdown.

Search: NVIDIA says channel counts divisible by 8 suffice for fp16 tensor cores, so Cin=24 is aligned. E043 puts half of the freeze saving in fused memory-bound kernels, and conv1 is only ~6% of forward MACs. Members lean refuted.
Prior lowered by NVIDIA guidance and E043 (high overall conv throughput). Still cheap to settle with a per-layer trace.

Padding 24→32 reaches neither the tensor-core requirement (already met at 8) nor the 64/256 tiling sweet spot, and adds 33% to conv1 MACs. Members expect refutation 3–1. Kept open only because it is math-identical and cheap, so it should run only on a reproducible build (H4.1.5), where it can be judged with no noise.
Pending. The baseline must be E036 on seeds 13–32 in the same build session, not E044 k0.

new.statement: The rebuild spread comes from autotune/cudagraph kernel reselection, not within-build nondeterminism. (1) Running one built E036 artifact twice in the same process on seeds 0–2 gives bit-identical per-seed accuracies. (2) Building E036 with mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' (or max-autotune with a persisted, pinned autotune cache) twice in fresh processes gives bit-identical per-seed accuracies, at a time cost of ≤1% vs E036. If (1) fails, nondeterministic kernels (e.g. cuDNN wgrad) are the source and pinning will not help.

Seed 1's persistent ~0.3 pp deficit is tied to its weight init. Offline on the E036 tip: holding seed 1's data/augmentation RNG fixed and redrawing only the init (10 draws) gives a mean ≥0.2 pp above seed 1's usual ~0.750. Holding seed 1's init fixed and redrawing only the data RNG (10 draws) gives a mean ≤0.751. This is diagnostic only and must never be exploited by reordering RNG draws.

The 0.19 pp gap between seeds 3–12 and 13–22 is winner's curse, not seed-set difficulty. Run E027 (commit 3735f58), which no decision on 13–22 selected, offline on seeds 13–22. Its mean stays within 0.08 pp of its seeds 3–12 mean (0.7526). If it instead drops ≥0.15 pp, the gap is seed-set difficulty and post-hoc discounts must be withdrawn.

Re-measuring the epoch dial on the E036 tip: +0.25 true epoch (~231→~237 steps; resolution, LR, Lookahead, detach and freeze kept as step fractions) raises the 20-seed mean on seeds 13–32, against E036 on the same seeds in the same build session, by 0.06–0.15 pp for +0.10–0.18 s. That puts the post-freeze dial at ~0.8–2 s/pp and buys margin toward the 0.7545 gate.

Decisive test for H2.6.8, where members are split. On the E036 tip, a group-2 freeze over the last 10% of steps (E046's recipe) combined with a +0.25 true epoch top-up gives a mean time at least 2% below E036. Its 20-seed mean (seeds 13–32) is within 0.03 pp of, or above, E036 run on the same seeds in the same build session. If the group-2 freeze alone loses ≥0.15 pp in that same-build pairing, the cascade is no better than the dial.

The memory-bound fused BN/GELU/pointwise kernels (27% of a 32 px step, E043) can be shrunk only by using fewer or cheaper elementwise layers, because Inductor cannot fold training-mode BN into a conv epilogue. Activations with cheaper backward passes, or removing a BN/activation from the residual path, cut per-step time roughly in proportion to the activation bytes removed.

On the E036 tip, replacing GELU with ReLU in the conv groups (keeping GELU, if any, before group 1, as in Hiverge, which uses SiLU) cuts mean time by at least 3%. It loses no more than 0.15 pp of the 20-seed mean on seeds 13–32 against a same-build E036 baseline. ReLU's backward needs only a sign mask, so the fused backward reads less.

Backward truncation in any group saves about 1.5–2× that group's backward FLOP share, because a frozen block also skips its BN/GELU backward (memory-bound), its Muon/SGD update and its Lookahead traffic. This explains both counterexamples: E028 saved 27% of a 32 px step against a ~12% FLOP share, and E046 saved ~10 ms per frozen step, beating every forecast. Per-group freeze value should therefore be estimated from profiled time, not MACs.

A torch.profiler trace of E046's group-2-frozen 32 px step against E036's group-1-frozen step shows a saving of ≥8 ms, with ≥30% of it in fused BN/GELU/pointwise kernels and a measurable drop in optimizer (Muon NS plus update) time.

The airbench96 width allocation is CIFAR-10-tuned. Capacity on small maps (group 3, at 7×7 and 3×3) costs little time per MAC on this step (E021: time scaled sublinearly with MACs on small maps; E043: conv kernels are efficient), while the 100-way task may be capacity-limited late in the network. Moving capacity toward group 3 raises accuracy per second better than the epoch dial.

On the E036 tip, widening group 3 from 512 to 640 channels (Muon lr unchanged, every graph recaptured) raises the 20-seed mean on seeds 13–32 by at least 0.15 pp against a same-build E036 baseline, for at most +2.5% time. That rate (≤~0.9 s/pp) would beat the dial. E010's 576→512 narrowing (−0.25 pp for −4.8%) is the counter-prior.

Ghost BatchNorm: on the E036 tip, computing BN statistics over 4 ghost sub-batches of 500 (a reshape inside the compiled graph, running stats unchanged in eval) raises the 20-seed mean on seeds 13–32 by at least 0.15 pp against a same-build baseline, for at most +3% time. The prior is low because E016/E022 suggest the recipe is over- rather than under-regularized.

structured_output.summary: Revised the tree after E043–E046, the search results and the review. Bookkeeping: H1.3.6 refuted (E044's paired test found no effect from BN recalibration), and the BN-mixture caveat was dropped from H1.3. H4.3.1 refuted, since three builds of the same E036 commit gave seeds 0–2 means of 0.7532, 0.7525 and 0.7497. H4.1 rewritten to cover the 0.35 pp rebuild spread, the persistent seed-1 deficit (probably tied to init) and the open question of winner's curse vs seed-set difficulty. H4 and H1 headlines restated: the unselected population is ~0.7535, local pass probability is ≤50%, and there is one fixed keep gate. H1 confidence lowered, since no accuracy-per-epoch booster has held up since E016. E043 settles H2.2.4 by calculation (conv kernels run well above 90 TFLOP/s), refutes H6.1/H6.1.1 (24 px step time is pixel-proportional), supports H6.3, and caps Muon levers at ~2.5% of a step (H1.2.3 retired, H1.2.2 re-scoped). Search lowers H6.4/H6.4.2 (Cin=24 is already tensor-core aligned) and bears on H1.5.4 (the reference renormalizes filters) and on H4.3 (PCIe specs). H2.3.8's invalid cross-seed comparison was withdrawn. E045's rate was corrected to ~1.5 s/pp, the same as the dial. H4.2's dial slope was flagged as stale. H2.6.8 marked inconclusive. H2.4 retired. New items: build reproducibility (H4.1.5), seed-1 init diagnostic (H4.1.6), winner's-curse vs seed-set test (H4.4.2), dial re-measure and margin top-up on the tip (H4.2.6), a decisive same-build test for the group-2 freeze plus top-up (H2.6.9), the memory-bound elementwise share with a GELU→ReLU test (H6.5/H6.5.1), and truncation saving 1.5–2× its FLOP share, which explains the E028/E046 counterexamples (H6.6/H6.6.1). Also new: capacity moved to group 3 (H1.7/H1.7.1) and ghost BN (H1.5.9). The other counterexamples are accounted for: E043's accuracy by rebuild noise, E030/E032 by the averaging local optimum in H1.3, and E031's time by its uncertain base (H2.7). Recommended next steps: make builds reproducible (H4.1.5), then buy margin (H4.2.6), then run cuts against same-build baselines on seeds 13–32.
